output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with careful reasoning: the evidence is already strongly discriminating between the rival explanations, so extra collection was unnecessary.
output.brief: The August dip is almost entirely explained by the failure of the chiller serving floors 6-8 from 4 to 19 August. Those floors' room-comfort score fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4, and recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Of the 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 were flat overall, and cleanliness and check-in scores did not move on any floor. Inspection pass rates stayed at 95-96% under the new contractor. Kiosk use and queue times were stable. The survey method was unchanged. So do not give notice to Orrin or pull the kiosks. The evidence does not support either move. Don't drop the floor 6-8 responses either, because that would hide a real failure. Restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a cooling-outage guest-recovery protocol. The outage guests already received an apology and credit, so a return-stay offer is optional. The 6% rate rise can't be separated from the usual August value dip. Keep watching value scores before reversing it. I'm fairly confident in this, and I collected no further evidence.
